mechanism: Replace the quadratic query-graph edge objective with Huber edge energy. Small contrasts retain quadratic curvature; large contrasts exert bounded forces, limiting the pull of strong nonlocal connections across a foreground/background contrast.

input_contract.y: Frozen MEAN pre-graph target s+0.25*(rank(unit(reference-FG-mean) cosine)-rank(s)), not the already-smoothed MEAN output
input_contract.graph: Same frozen reciprocal 20-NN query cosine graph, unique undirected edges and mean weighted degree normalization
input_contract.constant_source_exception: A constant original score follows the existing empty-output contract upstream; do not synthesize ranked reference corrections for that exception
input_contract.resource: Existing frozen DINO caches, no new encoder forward, no query GT/class/fold inference input
input_contract.binding_status: Both pre-graph NPZ and raw q/r/cov/score reconstruction supported. Synthetic reconstructed quadratic control agrees with existing MEAN within 2.98e-8; actual cohort binding and numerical check not yet performed.

steps: Read the frozen pre-graph target/fidelity and canonical undirected query graph from a CPU NPZ packet; open only y,a,edge_i,edge_j,edge_w. Alternatively open only q,r,cov,score and reconstruct the locked MEAN pre-graph inputs on CPU.
Solve the boxed convex problem with an incidence-operator primal-dual iteration. The dual proximal operation divides by 1+sigma/(16*w), then clips to +/-16*w*0.05.
Compute a feasible dual lower bound and primal upper bound every 25 iterations. Stop at gap/token<=1e-8; reject uncertified output at 20000 iterations.
Bilinear upsample the resulting field to 1024 and threshold strictly above 0.5; no new min-max or CRF.
Save same-input/same-readout boxed quadratic, original unboxed quadratic and pre-graph controls. These are controls of this one method, not additional method counts.
Seal prediction completion before any query-GT scoring; retain repeated occurrences and record input/source/prediction hashes.

prediction.conditional: If incorrect propagation is caused by strong graph connections across a real object/background contrast, force saturation can preserve the contrast while smoothing smaller within-object variations.
proved: A single edge contributes at most 16*w*0.05 in magnitude to either endpoint's gradient
If every optimized edge contrast stays at most 0.05, the Huber objective coincides with the same boxed quadratic objective
Strictly positive fidelity makes the boxed objective strongly convex with a unique minimizer
Feasible primal-dual gap bounds coordinate error by sqrt(2*gap/a_i); threshold signs outside this margin are certified
The conservative incidence-norm step bound satisfies the required strict primal-dual step inequality

counterexamples: A wrong object whose source score is already high can retain that high score more strongly; saturation can protect an error.
Useful recovery sometimes requires smoothing across a large score contrast; Huber may block it.
Many misleading edges can exert a large aggregate force even though each edge is bounded.
An isolated or badly connected object cannot obtain new supporting information from this objective.
Reference misidentification present in y is not resolved by this optimizer alone.
